title: Derived Hom from any nonzero bounded coherent complex over a complete local ring detects zero
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with $\mathfrak m$ its unique proper maximal ideal. Suppose $R$ is complete, meaning that $R\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R/\mathfrak m^n$ is an isomorphism. Work in the ordinary module derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], realized on the one-object ringed site. Write $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ for objects whose cohomology is zero outside a finite interval and is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] in every degree. Use the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For every nonzero $C\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ and every $Z\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$,
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,Z)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Z=0.$$
There is no scalar-action, finite projective dimension, or finite injective dimension assumption on $C$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-complete-local-coherent-duality] to the complete Noetherian local ring $R$. Fix its $\Omega$ and write $\mathbb D(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,\Omega)$. Put $W=\mathbb D(Z)$. Since $Z\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$, the cited boundedness-preservation clause gives $W\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$, and its canonical biduality clause gives $Z\simeq\mathbb D(W)$.

proof.text: Both $C$ and $W$ have bounded-above finitely generated cohomology. By the closure clause of [lem-trf-local-derived-tensor-nonvanishing], $T=C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}W$ belongs to $D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$. In particular it belongs to $D_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$, even though it need not be bounded below.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent; local coherent tensor-closure corollary stated in the cited node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-bimodule-tensor-hom] to the identity map $S=B=R$, with $(X,E,V)=(C,W,\Omega)$. Restriction of scalars is the identity and its $J_W(\Omega)$ is $\mathbb D(W)$: the specified action $(rh)(w)=h(rw)=r h(w)$ is the ordinary $R$-action on Hom. Its derived isomorphism and Step 1 give $$\mathbb D(T)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,\mathbb D(W))\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,Z)=0.$$ The replacement of the target along biduality uses functoriality of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: Tag 0A65, lemma-internal-hom; equivalently dga.tex Tags 09LN, lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, and 09LT, lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint, with all rings equal to R.

proof.text: Apply the unbounded coherent biduality clause of [lem-trf-complete-local-coherent-duality] to $T$ from Step 2. Step 3 gives $T\simeq\mathbb D\mathbb D(T)\simeq\mathbb D(0)=0$; the last equality follows by taking the zero source complex in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The zero-detection clause of [lem-trf-local-derived-tensor-nonvanishing] now gives $C=0$ or $W=0$. As $C\ne0$, we have $W=0$. Biduality for $Z$ from Step 1 therefore gives $Z\simeq\mathbb D(W)=\mathbb D(0)=0$.
